credits: Award announcements by the IEEE Computer Society Technical Community on Security and Privacy (IEEE S&P), USENIX, ACM SIGSAC (CCS) and the NDSS Symposium.
method: Sources. Every entry comes from the conference's own award announcement: the award pages of IEEE S&P, USENIX's Best Papers list and the USENIX Security programs, the ACM SIGSAC award history and the CCS award pages, and the NDSS Symposium pages and award slides (NDSS 2016 from the Internet Society's announcement). Each entry links to the page it came from.
Years. IEEE S&P from 2008, USENIX Security from 2001, ACM CCS from 2013 and NDSS from 2016, the first years with award lists on the official sites, through 2026.

Awards included. Best Paper and Distinguished Paper awards, plus the Best Student Paper and Best Practical Paper awards that IEEE S&P and USENIX Security gave in some years. Honorable mentions, runners-up, artifact awards, poster awards and Test of Time awards are not included. USENIX's 2026 Best Papers list also includes five Distinguished Artifact winners; they are left out.

Award names. The name of the top award differs between conferences and changes over time. IEEE S&P called it Outstanding Paper in 2008, Best Paper in 2009–2014 and 2020–2021, and Distinguished Paper in 2015–2019 and since 2022. USENIX Security gave Best Paper and Best Student Paper awards until 2016 (Outstanding Paper in 2009 and 2011) and Distinguished Paper awards since 2017. CCS gave Best Paper awards until 2019 and in 2021, and Distinguished Paper awards in 2020 and since 2022. NDSS gave Distinguished Paper awards, except in 2026 (Best Paper). The badges keep each conference's name; hover over one to see the exact wording.

Authors and links. Authors are as listed on the award page; where it gives only initials (CCS 2024), they come from the conference's accepted-papers page. A few obvious misspellings of names were corrected. Titles link to a free PDF when one was found (278 of 401 papers): the official PDF on usenix.org or ndss-symposium.org, and for IEEE S&P and CCS a free copy found through OpenAlex (the ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, arXiv or a university repository). Papers without a free PDF link to their DOI or paper page and to a Google Scholar search.

Topics and types. Each paper was given one of the 21 topics used on the Top Security PIs page and one of seven types of paper by a language model reading its title. "LLM-related" marks papers on LLM and AI security and papers that use LLMs. These labels are rough; many papers fit more than one.
